headline: Binance now expects withdrawals back in about 40 hours and promises a full Proof of Reserves by Monday, while crypto stocks fall 7-12% alongside a tech sell-off.

market.asOf: Read from CoinDesk's live blog entry at 13:43 UTC Fri 30 Oct (20:43 Bangkok), not a live price page: CoinGecko, CoinMarketCap and the Fear & Greed index could not be opened this run, and no ETH or SOL reading with a time was found. Check the live prices at the top of the page.
market.fearGreed: Not read this run: the index page could not be opened.

stories.title: Binance: withdrawals expected in about 40 hours, full Proof of Reserves by Monday
stories.summary: Co-CEO Richard Teng said in a video on X that Binance is rebuilding its withdrawal service and will only reopen it after strict tests, now expected in about 40 hours. A full Proof of Reserves report (a public check that customer balances are fully backed) is due by Monday at the latest. Teng says only Binance's own hot wallet was hit and customer funds were not touched.
points: The attacker used Ethereum's EIP-7702 feature to take control of a Binance hot wallet, skipping Binance's normal approval process, per TechFlow.
Binance has set aside more than $6.34B, of which about $5B is already held in the affected assets, per CoinDesk.
Sources differ on the size: Chainalysis puts the theft at about $6.4B with about $2.8B frozen; CoinDesk puts it at about $6.3B, and a Binance spokesperson says about $3B is frozen.
Chainalysis says the attacker swapped $325M of stablecoins for $285M of ETH in about 20 minutes, and attributes the attack to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

stories.title: Crypto stocks fall 7-12% as the hack lands on top of a tech sell-off
stories.summary: At the US open, crypto company shares fell much harder than bitcoin itself, as the Binance hack hit at the same time as a broad drop in tech stocks.
points: At 13:43 UTC Coinbase was down 12% at $140.13 and Strategy down 11% at $132.57, while bitcoin was $76,800, down 4% in 24 hours, per CoinDesk.
Circle fell 9.5%, Bullish 8.3% and Galaxy 6.8%; the Nasdaq was down more than 2% and Intel fell 28% after weak guidance, per CoinDesk.
Coinbase's bitcoin price premium fell to one of its deepest discounts since early 2023, a sign US buyers are selling harder than others, per CoinDesk.
Standard Chartered's Geoffrey Kendrick sees no new base until frozen assets are released and more detail of the hack emerges, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: CoinDesk: Standard Chartered sees more losses ahead

stories.title: US wage growth slows and Chicago factory index misses
stories.summary: Two US reports this morning came in calm or soft. Higher interest rates usually weigh on crypto, so softer data makes a December Fed rate hike a little less certain.
points: Employment costs rose 0.8% in Q3 (wages +0.7%, benefits +0.9%) and 3.4% over 12 months, per the BLS.
Chicago PMI fell to 55.3 against 56.1 expected and 58.8 the month before; above 50 still means growth, per Newsquawk.
Before the data, odds of a December hike had fallen to about 70% from nearly 90%, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Hacker sells altcoins for ETH, and ENA falls
briefs.summary: The attacker sold 217.5M ENA, 7.02M UNI and 7.77T PEPE among other tokens for 70,480 ETH (about $158.25M), per Lookonchain; ENA fell 7.26%.

briefs.title: A little-known 2017 token crashes 90% after a hacker sale
briefs.summary: The hacker sold 134.1M FUN into a very thin trading pool and the price fell more than 90% on Uniswap.

briefs.title: Aave reopens its markets
briefs.summary: Aave reopened its V3 and V4 markets after a precautionary freeze; USDT, USDC, XAUT and PAXG are temporarily barred as collateral for new loans. Aave says it was not affected by the hack.

briefs.title: Polymarket's international platform breached
briefs.summary: A compromised third-party provider let attackers drain user accounts; DefiLlama tracked about $2.7M in losses. Polymarket says users will be made whole and halted trading.

briefs.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows slow to $17.07M
briefs.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in $17.07M on 29 Oct, a fourth straight day of inflows but about 88% less than the day before.
